SATOM 2.11.0

A large security and consistency release — every page and action now enforces its own permission, passwords and idle sessions follow one policy, privileged actions are audited, and a long list of everyday problems is fixed.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user

Released: 2026-10-03 · All releases

In short#

2.11.0 is a hardening and clean-up release. Its main theme is that what you see is what you may do: every page, button and menu entry now checks the same permission, pages that used to open for any signed-in user now ask for a view permission, and rows hidden from a list can no longer be reached by typing their address. Passwords follow one rule everywhere, the Session Lock setting finally signs idle browsers out, and privileged node actions now leave an audit trail.

Alongside the security work come a few new tools (external change approval, secret values for integration hooks, store snapshots on the Collection page, Clear all for notifications), safer restore and firmware paths, and a long list of fixes across change requests, scheduled actions, monitoring, the FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer consoles and the Tools menu.

The three built-in profiles (Read-only, Operator and Admin) keep the access they had. If you use custom profiles, read Before you upgrade.

What's new#

Change control and integrations#

  • Record an external approval. A change request in External approval mode could never run, because nothing recorded the outside verdict. Your integrations can now send the verdict to SATOM through the REST API (with an administrator-scope token; changes outside the token's workspace are not found; manual-mode and closed changes are refused; every call is audited). An Administrator can also record or withdraw the verdict by hand on the change's External change record card. See Change requests.
  • Change ticket reference from a hook. When a hook that runs on a new change request succeeds and returns a ticket reference (and optionally a link), SATOM now stores it on the change request, as the starter and the Request CRQ message always promised. A link that is not a web address is dropped, a closed change is left alone, and the run's status says whether the reference was recorded.
  • Secret values for hooks. The hook editor has a new write-only Secret values card for Administrators. You can give each secret a hook declares its value; it is stored encrypted, audited by name and never shown again (the card only says stored or not set). Before, secrets could only come from the node's environment. See Integrations.

Notifications#

  • The Notifications page has a Clear all button. After you confirm, it permanently deletes all your notifications. The bell's Clear still only marks them read. See Notifications.

Monitoring#

  • Peer replication status on the Collection page: whether this node's samples are also written to the peer node, which peer, the last success and the number of failures in a row.
  • Store snapshots and nodes: a new card shows the state of each node's metrics store and lists its snapshots. Users with edit rights can take or delete a snapshot; deleting one is audited. See Metrics collection.
  • Unmute is now available on muted probes in Deep monitors and Service Monitor.
  • Analytics boards can be created from the page and open straight away, and custom boards gain an Edit board form for the title, description, default range and auto-refresh. Built-in boards stay read-only and keep Duplicate.
  • Period reports now show their fleet section (minimum, average and maximum per device and metric, policies that were down, collectors that failed) on the page, in the plain-text and e-mail body and in the CSV export — not only in the JSON export. If the metrics store could not be reached, the report says so.

Administration#

  • Users page actions. Each user row now offers Reset password (local accounts, with confirmation), Clear 2FA (when enabled) and Unlock (when the account has failed sign-ins or is locked out). All three are audited. Unlock clears the lockout and nothing else: a disabled account stays disabled. Holders of View users now get a read-only user list and a Users entry in the sidebar. See Users and permission profiles.
  • Node TLS renewal. Settings → Node TLS has a new Renewal of an imported certificate card: choose Alert only or Automatic pull, enter where to fetch the certificate from, and press Test now. Renew now is offered only for certificates issued by the internal CA, and the page explains that an imported certificate is shared between HA nodes. See Node TLS.
  • Create backup now on System Backup can push the bundle to the backup server (ticked by default when one is configured).

Tools#

  • False-positive explainer: two optional fields — a Web Protection Profile, now named in the "where on the device" path under each carve-out, and a payload decoder that peels encoding layers off a value you paste without a log entry. See False-positive explainer.
  • Certificate inspector: the Paste tab has a passphrase field for encrypted private keys, and the Probe tab an optional SNI / host name field. See Certificate inspector.

What changes for you#

One password policy#

There is now one rule everywhere: at least 12 and at most 1024 characters, length only, with no rule about character classes. It applies to Add User, an administrator's password reset, Change Password, the reset link, the operator CLI's password reset, the installer and the guided setup. Before, each of these had its own rule, and the web forms accepted any non-empty password while saying "at least 8 characters". Existing passwords are not checked again; the rule applies the next time a password is set.

Session Lock now signs idle browsers out#

Settings → General → Session Lock (minutes) was saved but never applied, so a browser could stay signed in for weeks. It is now an idle timeout: a browser with no activity for that long is signed out on its next click with "Your session was locked after N minutes of inactivity.", and the lock is written to the audit log. Background refreshes (the notification bell, job progress, status badges, edit-lock heartbeats and timed panel reloads) do not count as activity, so a tab left open still locks. API tokens are not affected. See General settings.

Pages and actions ask for the right permission#

  • Read pages need a view permission. About 80 pages only checked that you were signed in. Now the audit trail needs View audit log; the API consoles of FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator need View registry; the appliance list and detail pages need View appliances; Device Provisioning needs View operations; and the Monitoring pages need any read permission. The Audit Log menu entry follows its page's permission.
  • Device-content pages need a view permission. The FortiWeb workspace, protection pages, exceptions, WAF artifacts, server objects, the other product workspaces, the API registry, Sentinel and the network tools now require the matching view permission. The Global home lists appliances only to holders of View appliances.
  • Rows hidden from a list stay hidden. Device lists only show what you may see (maintenance devices need View maintenance devices; each workspace shows only its own product). About thirty pages and actions skipped that rule, so a hidden row was one address away. They now answer "not found". This covered carve-outs, template apply, AppID assignment, Stored Assets, firmware reports and downloads, the REST API, bulk System Provisioning and baseline apply (which could write to every appliance instead of the visible ones), Upgrade Flow, Analysis, Log Collection, process runs, the calendar, edit locks, plugins, Lua scripts, the Python Console, Sentinel incidents and the endpoint registry.
  • Firmware upgrade, boot-partition switch, upgrade scheduling and HA failover need Run appliance actions; before, any edit permission was enough.
  • Raw writes through the internal appliance relay need Execute write API calls, the same permission the API Explorer asks for. Reads are unchanged.
  • Refresh from device on Server Policy and Server Objects runs a full sync and now needs configuration edit rights, like the same button elsewhere.
  • Fetch MAC addresses on the Architecture device card needs edit rights, is audited, and is hidden from users who cannot use it.
  • The AI opinion on a draft exception needs the AI Advisor permission. SATOM's own analysis stays open to anyone who can open the exception. The Attack ID page shows its AI buttons only to holders of that permission.
  • Edit locks: taking, keeping or taking over a lock needs configuration rights, so a read-only user can no longer take an operator's lock. Saves and deletes in the object editor are refused while someone else holds the lock, and the inline editor on configuration pages now takes and shows the lock too. See Edit locks.
  • Sentinel and Scout settings can only be saved by user administrators, matching who could see the panes.
  • API tokens can no longer be created or edited with a scope their owner does not hold.
  • Scout's "Published host" is dialled only if the appliance publishes that host, unless you hold the free-target probe permission or manage users. Leaving the field blank works as before.
  • Database tools refuse any query, CSV export or report widget that touches a credential table (users, API tokens, application settings, hypervisor targets, DNS backends, provisioning runs). The refusal is audited. See Database tools.
  • Plugin drafts and previews follow the Plugin Studio permission instead of requiring full administrator rights.

Backups and restore#

  • View backups now opens the Device Backups list (details only), so read-only users can see which backups exist. Creating, uploading and deleting still need a backup create or restore permission; downloading a backup (the full device configuration) needs Create backups.
  • The appliance Restore page needs both Manage users and Restore backups; Import Backup needs Restore backups. Operators and administrators keep their access.
  • Upgrade Preparation is granted by Run appliance actions.
  • A live restore is aborted when the automatic pre-restore backup fails, so a restore never runs without a rollback copy by accident. If the device cannot make that backup, tick Restore without a pre-restore backup; the choice is audited. See Configuration restore.
  • Boot Partition stays the emergency path with no change request, but a live flash now needs an acknowledgement that it bypasses change control, and every attempt is audited.

Firmware and Upgrade Flow#

  • The Schedule for later card on the single-appliance Upgrade page is gone: the action it created could never run. Use Upgrade Flow, which raises a change request with its window and schedules the upgrade once approved. Existing scheduled entries are left as they are.
  • Upgrade Flow now covers FortiWeb only, because SATOM cannot flash FortiADC; FortiADC pre-upgrade checks are still on the appliance page. See Upgrade Flow.

AI Advisor#

  • Every message that leaves the node is redacted. Before, only the newest message was; up to 19 earlier turns went out verbatim. Every turn sent is now redacted, counted in the export log and in the pre-send review, which says how many earlier messages go with the new one.
  • Local means a local address. An Ollama provider counted as local because of its type alone, even on a public host, skipping redaction, the "Allow external providers" switch and the export log. Now only loopback, link-local and private addresses (or localhost) count as local; a name that does not resolve counts as external. Change-request document translation follows the same rule.
  • New installations create the default Ollama provider disabled, pointing at the local machine. Set your Ollama host in Settings → AI Advisor and save it to enable it; until then the advisor, document translation and the exception assistant say the provider is disabled. Existing providers are unchanged. See AI Advisor settings.
  • Sentinel's AI endpoint now ships empty, and AI reasoning stays off until one is configured.

FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator consoles#

  • The FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer API consoles are dry-run by default, like FortiAuthenticator: a write shows the exact request and sends nothing until you tick Apply.
  • All three consoles audit every applied write, including writes the device refused, and no longer audit reads. An applied FortiAnalyzer write can now explain a configuration change.
  • All products save their endpoint catalog the same way, so names, addresses and duplicates are checked alike. Re-pointing a disabled FortiAuthenticator endpoint no longer re-enables it, enabled ones can be disabled, and its write methods are greyed out for users without Execute write API calls.

See Product API pages.

Menus and sidebar#

  • Appliances moved from the Administrator group into each workspace's Fleet group (and the Global group of the Global workspace), and anyone who can view appliances sees it. Adding or editing a device still needs configuration rights.
  • Process has its own Automation group and is visible to read-only users and operators.
  • Collection appears at the end of the Monitoring menu for operators who can edit collection settings.
  • Device Console is in the Automation menu for operators.
  • Template Library appears under Operations for users with operations view rights who are not administrators.
  • Studio entries (Python Console, Plugin Studio, Lua Studio) in the Global workspace have their own group, and each is shown only to holders of its permission.
  • The FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator menus show their console under API → Registry & console to everyone with View registry. The FortiADC Signatures overview moved to the Web Application Firewall group and opens with View protection.
  • The sidebar, top-bar search and home shortcuts check a page's permission before showing a link, so you are never offered a page that then refuses you. Log Collection, firmware, boot-partition and failover buttons are hidden from users who cannot use them.
  • The firmware library is no longer reachable from the FortiADC and FortiAuthenticator workspaces, nor the backup vault from FortiAuthenticator: neither could flash or back up those devices.

Read-only users see read-only pages#

Users without configuration edit rights no longer see buttons that would only fail: on Server Policy, the policy editor, Exceptions, Web Protection, Server Objects and WAF artifacts. Some are greyed out instead of hidden, and the policy editor says it is read-only. The SSH console shows presets with a read-only notice instead of a Run button to users who cannot run commands. On the Appliances pages, Add, Edit, Delete and View Backups appear only to those who hold the permission. On Collection and Analysis, the run, save and edit controls follow the same rule. A system profile can only be deployed live once approved, and Approve/Reject appear only to approvers.

Settings and administration#

  • Log Levels and Log Format in General settings now take effect at start-up and on save (plain, detailed or JSON lines). The unused Status Poll Interval and Show raw JSON fields were removed.
  • The Profiles tab needs Manage profiles; Certificate Manager links appear only to users who can open it; the API Tokens link appears in every workspace whose product supports tokens; revoking or deleting a token asks for confirmation; logo and favicon pickers accept every supported format; the static "Security Status" checklist is gone; the HA diagram no longer shows replication on a standalone node.
  • The seeded nightly system-backup schedule on new installations no longer names a specific backup host.
  • The daily inventory snapshot that feeds the Metrics page trend is now part of the seeded schedule (daily at 23:50), and the installation check lists it among the minimum protections. Existing schedules are never changed.
  • Examples and placeholders across the console (DNS Lookup, the probe form, installation health) use generic values instead of names from the network the product was built on.

Wording#

  • The Rediscovery Stop tooltip explains that a stop keeps the snapshot already saved; capacity messages match the checks and the capacity table highlights usage at your warning level instead of a fixed 80 percent; "Network Segments" has one name everywhere; the "Run appliance actions" and "Restore backups" descriptions say what they unlock.
  • Appliances pages show Policy Inspector and Rediscovery on FortiADC rows too, show Firmware Reports consistently, and label the vdom field "ADOM (vdom)". The Device Provisioning mode table describes what Full and DHCP modes really do.
  • The Naming page marks FortiADC patterns as reference only; the FortiAnalyzer workspace is no longer described as a scaffold; the FortiAuthenticator dashboard points to Administrator → Appliances; Fleet Objects says its data comes from SATOM's local copy of each configuration; the classification catalog counts line profiles where a value is used.

Fixed#

Change requests#

  • Only a draft change request can be approved. Approving a finished change used to set it back to approved, notify integrations again and rebuild its rollout plan. A completed, failed or cancelled change can no longer be cancelled.
  • Schedule after the window has started now starts the run a minute later instead of creating a task that never fires; after the window has closed it is refused.
  • A firmware upgrade or failover run from an appliance page closes its change only when every appliance in it has a result; a failed appliance can be retried inside the window.
  • A rollout in several rounds stays open until the last round succeeds, and a failed round stops the rest. The Schedule button honours the saved rollout plan; a change with no appliance can no longer be raised or scheduled.
  • Documentary changes (and changes still running after their window) can be closed with Mark completed / Mark failed.
  • Mark notified sends the notice to the change's own recipients.
  • The window opening and closing hook events fire even without NetBox, with the documented outcome.
  • A firmware change page states that the scheduler does not flash firmware; appliances are flashed live from their Upgrade page.

Integrations#

  • The four hook starters (CRM change ticket, Telegram, Slack, Microsoft Teams) never actually ran, yet their runs showed ok. They now run and report a failed answer from the receiving system as a failed run, with its message.

Scheduled actions#

  • A one-time Run at is entered and shown in the console time zone; it used to be read as UTC and fired at the wrong hour. Next run shows its time zone, and a run skipped while the scheduler was down shows as missed.
  • The running badge shows while an action actually runs. Action descriptions are corrected (NetBox Appliances per round, FortiAuthenticator in the sync actions, the 3-minute deep-monitor sweep).

Appliances, firmware and backups#

  • Quick edit wiped interfaces and HA settings. Saving from the Edit dialog on the Appliances list deleted every documented interface and dissolved an HA cluster. The quick edit now leaves them alone.
  • Upgrade and Boot Partition pickers no longer offer installation images, which are not flash payloads.
  • A second rediscovery can no longer start while the first is still running, and starting one no longer cancels a pending Stop.
  • A FortiADC discovery with refused credentials stops after one failed sign-in instead of risking an account lockout.
  • Device health grades each appliance with its own product's limits, the same the alert engine uses; the hardware scan targets FortiWeb only.
  • "View Backups" for a FortiADC from the Global workspace no longer ends on "not found". Deleting an appliance through the REST API now cleans up like the delete button.
  • Device Console presets and support-bundle diagnostics now match the appliance's product instead of always sending FortiWeb commands.
  • Adding or removing a model on Capacity Limits affects only the product you chose.
  • Stored Assets shows "unknown" with the reason when the backup server cannot be read, instead of "never pushed", and long folders say "Showing the N newest of M files".

Provisioning, policies and templates#

  • Device Provisioning shows a refused preflight as an error instead of "Nothing blocks this run"; Semi mode's Resume carries on to registration and profile.
  • System Provisioning no longer promises secrets "entered at apply time": secrets are removed when a profile is saved and are not pushed, and the preview names what goes out without them. Combos now push their profiles' settings.
  • Line profiles saved from the Global workspace never reached the line wizard, leaving its profile list empty. They are now filed as FortiWeb profiles and earlier ones are moved over.
  • The line wizard uses your naming patterns, attaches the certificate it issues to the new policy, and checks that the line's protection profile exists before reserving anything.
  • New Server Policy includes the protection profile field and assigns the chosen AppID; bulk clones keep your suffix; the delete dialog says which objects are deleted with the policy; "Change Appliance" opens the device map.
  • Approving a protection template deploys it to FortiWeb devices only, and the canary is the first device you selected.
  • Config Compare exports every differing field; the AppIDs header option works; the Structure firmware selector works again (administrators only).

Monitoring and search#

  • Global Search ignored its Appliance and Object Type filters. They now apply and are kept on the results page.
  • New deep-monitor and Service Monitor probes default to 3 minutes, matching the sweep (5 minutes actually meant every 6). Existing probes keep their interval.
  • FortiADC device-wide response times no longer pose as per-service data in the Service drill-down.
  • The Audit Log pages again, its To date includes the whole day, and Export CSV downloads the filtered entries.

Settings and administration#

  • Hour thresholds saved with decimals were ignored by the alert engine; they are honoured now.
  • Enable email sending off now stops every outgoing mail; only Send test email still sends.
  • Deleting an ADOM asks for confirmation again, and so do deleting a process, a change type or a WAF artifact version (they used to delete without asking).
  • A new LDAP bind password works when a secrets vault is in use; saving Authentication no longer resets LDAP and RADIUS timeouts.
  • Certificate Manager over ACME no longer demands an ADCS template and records the request id for revocation.
  • Importing the same theme a third time no longer fails; built-in database reports offer Clone; SQL console export works before Run.
  • Re-enabling a FortiAnalyzer menu group brings its items back.
  • Code rollback obeys the staged-rollout safeguard, and container installations refuse rollback and offline packages with a reason.
  • Apply protocol & ciphers under Node TLS failed on most installations. It is now queued to the privileged updater, and the result appears under Software Update.
  • With a custom service account, the integration hook runner now uses it from the start, so hooks run on those installations.
  • The Naming page opens in the Global workspace, and Concept Map links to Global-only pages open there.

Products and tools#

  • FortiADC API console: in a translated interface, DELETE was sent as the translated word, bypassing the permission check. The real verb is now always sent; PATCH is offered.
  • FortiAnalyzer API console reports the device's real status and error instead of always 200.
  • FortiADC object editor: the first member of an empty pool can be added; registry edits reach every worker within a minute without a restart.
  • FortiAnalyzer Device Manager: Authorize and Delete run in the FortiAnalyzer ADOM you enter (default root); unusable buttons are gone.
  • Transaction tracer: users without the free-target permission can trace again; a backend typed without a scheme uses HTTPS only on ports 443 and 8443; leg A dials the recorded management port; leg B lists FortiWeb only; attack-log correlation matches the right source address.
  • Lua Studio: a real deploy without a target is refused instead of marked "deployed", and refusals show their reason.
  • Smaller fixes: "/" opens Search from any page; the infrastructure health card uses plain labels and points to the Backup Server settings; the profile page no longer accepts a hidden password change; the installer's standby hint points to High Availability → Add node.

Before you upgrade#

  • Plain HTTP was reachable after updates. On installed nodes, the application could answer plain HTTP from the network on its internal port after a self-update, next to the normal HTTPS endpoint. Installing this update replaces the service definition with one that listens on the local machine only; until then, the node stays exposed.
  • Review custom profiles. Pages and actions now require their own permission. The built-in Read-only, Operator and Admin profiles hold every permission needed, but a custom profile may lose access to pages it reached before. See Permissions.
  • Passwords: the next password set for any account must be 12 to 1024 characters.
  • Session Lock now signs idle browsers out. Check its value under Settings → General before users are surprised.
  • FortiADC response-time metrics were renamed to satom_adc_client_rtt_ms, satom_adc_server_rtt_ms and satom_adc_app_response_ms. Custom panels that queried the old names for FortiADC must switch; history under the old names stays where it is. See Metric series.
  • Regex lab rewrite numbering now follows FortiWeb and FortiADC: $0 is the first group. Rewrite strings written for the old preview ($1 for the first group) must be shifted down by one. See Regex lab.
  • Daily inventory snapshot: on an existing node, run the operator CLI's seed command (satom execute seed actions) to add it.
  • Scheduled firmware upgrades from the single-appliance page are gone; use Upgrade Flow.
  • The old development install script was removed. Use the supported installer or the guided setup. See Installation.

Under the hood#

  • Privileged node actions (system backup and restore, git bundle changes, firmware pull, code rollback, software update, HA changes and standby promotion, the root CLI's password reset and unlock) now write an audit entry with their outcome, and every failed local sign-in is logged.
  • The plugin frame no longer loads images from the web, closing a way for rendered data to leave the node.
  • An automatic check now refuses inline script handlers in pages, which the browser security policy was silently blocking.
  • Several unused endpoints and templates were removed (a raw device-read relay, an old exception delete, a firmware chunked upload, an AI Advisor attachment endpoint and an old Analysis dashboard).
